name: The Norwegian Childhood Cancer Biobank
description:
Pediatric cancer is the dominant cause of disease-related death in children over one year of age in Western countries. New treatment strategies are warranted, and rapid advancements in molecular and genetic sequencing technologies are realizing the potential for improving care through precision medicine. In pediatric oncology, this encompasses the identification of unique cancer predispositions, somatic tumor mutations, personalized surveillance, and targeted treatment.
The clinical benefits of these scientific advancements rely on the development of translational bioinformatic expertise, clinical pipelines for extended testing and services, and ethically sound information and decision systems for families and healthcare professionals within pediatric oncology.
The Norwegian Childhood Cancer Biobank was established in 2017 as a national initiative to support research and improve outcomes for children with cancer. The biobank collects and provides a broad range of high-quality biological samples, including plasma, serum, buffy coat, bone marrow, cerebrospinal fluid, urine, biopsy, feces, extracted tumor DNA and RNA, extracted genomic DNA (gDNA), and mononuclear cells (MNC) from leukemia patients.
Our goal is to use the generated knowledge toward the establishment of a general translational platform that integrates different molecular modalities, where novel molecular and genetic information is systematically translated into clinical application.
The biobank has also established an advisory board to guide its development and ensure its alignment with clinical and research needs.

name: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands (CeDNN)
description: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands, CeDNN, is collecting (bio)materials from celiac disease patients, relatives, partners and IBS patients. The aim is to get a better understanding of how CeD risk genes, the microbiome and environmental factors contribute to disease aetiology. To achieve this, a holistic approach will be applied in which we will study the behaviour of immune cells and the microbiome in CeD patients and compare that to non-patients using “omics” technology (i.e. the full repertoire of all transcripts, cytokine profiles, proteins, metabolites etc.) in the background of the genetic profile of each individual. To generate this information we will profile different immune cells from patients and controls. These datasets will be analysed and integrated using bioinformatics approaches to develop insights into the mechanisms underlying celiac disease. The hope is that the newly gained knowledge will contribute to disease prevention in patients with increased risk for developing celiac disease and to the discovery of novel treatment targets in patients that have developed disease already.

name: Microisolates in South Tyrol Study
description:
The MICROS Collection is a population based collection of biological samples and associated data established within the MICROS study (Microisolates in South Tyrol), a longitudinal genetic epidemiology study conducted in small, isolated populations in South Tyrol, Italy. 
The collection includes samples and data from adult participants recruited in three geographically and historically isolated communities (Stelvio, Martello and Vallelunga), with the aim of investigating the genetic structure of the population and the epidemiology of complex and Mendelian diseases. 
Biological materials collected comprise blood, urine and DNA, which are associated with a wide range of data including genealogical information, clinical measurements, and questionnaire-based data. The presence of extended genealogical records and large reconstructed pedigrees provides a unique framework for studying heritable traits and genetic determinants of disease in isolated populations. 
The collection was developed with a community-based recruitment approach and includes participants enrolled in the early 2000s, representing a well-characterised resource for genetic and epidemiological research. A subset of individuals from the MICROS study has subsequently been included in the CHRIS study, enabling continuity and integration with a larger population-based longitudinal cohort. 
Overall, the MICROS Collection represents a valuable resource for studying genetic architecture, population isolates, and disease mechanisms, supporting research in genetic epidemiology, complex trait analysis and translational biomedical science.

name: CHRIS COVID-19
description:
The CHRIS-Covid Collection is a disease specific collection of biological samples and associated data established during the SARS CoV 2 pandemic by the CHRIS Biobank (Eurac Research – Institute for Biomedicine) in collaboration with the local healthcare system of the Autonomous Province of Bolzano/Bozen. 
The collection is derived from the population based CHRIS cohort and represents a prospective extension focused on COVID 19, integrating newly collected data with pre existing longitudinal information from the cohort. 
It includes whole blood, serum and genomic DNA samples linked to epidemiological and clinical data from approximately 7,000 individuals, recruited within the CHRIS Covid study and related population-based investigations conducted in the region.
Samples are processed and stored according to the biobank’s standard operating procedures, ensuring quality and consistency. The collection supports epidemiological, clinical and genetic research on SARS CoV 2 infection, including studies on determinants of susceptibility and disease outcomes.
